description:
FILED s532b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-06) from #4166's measurement.  PRE-EXISTING.  LOW.

    open my $f, "<", "lib/FalseMod.pm"; -d "/nonexist"; my @l = <$f>; print "eof=", 0+$!, "\n";   # perl eof=0   PCL eof=2
    printf 'BEGIN { -d "/nonexist" } print "rt=", 0+$!, "\n";' > e3.pl; perl e3.pl                   # rt=0
    the same + a trailing `__END__` line                                                                # rt=2 (!)
    perl -e 'BEGIN { -d "/nonexist" }' -e 'print "rt=", 0+$!, "\n";'                                  # rt=2

perl: perlio.c:3174 (PerlIOUnix_read) `else if (len == 0 && count != 0) { PerlIOBase(f)->flags |= PERLIO_F_EOF; SETERRNO(0,0); }` -- a read that hits EOF clears errno.  The lexer reads a program FILE to its end, so a BEGIN-time ENOENT (a `use lib` whose -d checks miss, any failed stat in a BEGIN) is gone when the run phase starts -- unless the file stops at __END__/__DATA__ (no EOF read) or the program is -e.  PCL: `use lib 'lib'; print 0+$!` prints 2 (lib.pm's -d checks); perl 0.  #4166 fixed the half that mattered for exit statuses (a require that FINDS its file clears $!, pp_ctl.c S_require_file).  The fix shape: the readline / read / sysread / eof EOF arm clears *p-stored-errno* (%p-set-errno 0); the program-file half is the same rule applied once at the end of the main file's compile phase when its source has no __END__/__DATA__ -- probe both halves; the second is an artefact, decide whether to emulate it.


=== DONE (s536h) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, commit 89259b88, cl/ only).  Measured against perl's C (pp_sys.c, perlio.c) and 40 probe rows, all identical now:
- a RECORD read (readline scalar / list, any $/ mode) that reaches end of file clears $! -- %p-read-record asks %p-record-at-eof-p (no record, slurp, a short fixed record, a record its separator does not end; the per-line case is one char compare) and %p-note-read-eof clears errno the FIRST time a DESCRIPTOR stream hits EOF: perl's PERLIO_F_EOF is sticky (a second EOF read makes no read(2): `@a = <$h>; -d "/nope"; <$h>` keeps 2) until a seek (%p-seek-impl drops the stream from *p-eof-seen*, a weak table touched at EOF only).  An in-memory handle keeps $! (perl).
- read / sysread clear $! before they read (pp_sysread's SETERRNO(0,0): a read WITH data leaves 0 too), and so do syswrite (pp_syswrite) and truncate (pp_truncate, both forms) -- the same fact, probed.
- getc at end of file is EBADF (pp_getc's do_eof exit); eof() at end of file enters the EOF state and KEEPS $! (do_eof saves / restores errno), so a readline after it keeps $! too.
- THE LEXER CASE, emulated: perl's lexer reads a program FILE to its end, so p-run-compile-phase-blocks clears $! for the main program -- not for `-e` ($0 eq "-e") and not when the main program installed a __END__ / __DATA__ section (*p-main-data-section*, set by p-install-data-handle outside a unit load): `BEGIN { -d "/nope" } print 0+$!` is 0, with a trailing __END__ 2, as perl.
- `do FILE` that finds and opens its file clears $! (S_require_file's SETERRNO(0) serves do as it serves require -- #4166's twin, found by the probes).
Guard Pl/t/errno-magic-01.t rows 9-11 (rows 9-10 FAIL on the base; row 11, the __END__ control, passes on both).  Cost: see the s536h session-log paragraph (fhread / readline bench rows).
subject: A read that reaches END OF FILE leaves $! as it was in PCL; perl's PerlIO sets $! = 0 at EOF (perlio.c PerlIOUnix_read) -- `-d "/nope"; my @l = <$fh>; print 0+$!` is 0 in perl, 2 in PCL; the same EOF read is why a perl FILE program's run phase starts with $! = 0 after a BEGIN-time failure
